# Iteration 6 {.unnumbered}

This is the last iteration. You keep improving your models, make your final Kaggle submissions, and write down what you tried and what you learned.

## Apply what you read

In [Research to Practice](../../self-study/11_from_research_to_practice.qmd), the last activity of the Self-study, you chose at least one principle from a machine learning paper. Apply it to your project now: decide what you expect to change, run the experiment under your usual validation protocol, and record the result in your experiment log, also when it does not help.

## Compete, iterate, improve

There is no predefined end point. Continue moving through the CRISP-DM cycle as new questions emerge:

**understand → prepare → model → evaluate → learn → repeat**

You may revisit any part of the workflow, including:

* business and domain understanding
* data understanding
* data preparation
* feature engineering
* feature selection
* validation strategy
* model selection
* hyperparameter tuning
* classification
* regression
* clustering

There is no required order. For example, poor model performance may lead you back to data preparation. Clustering may reveal groups of molecules that behave differently. A validation score that does not agree with your Kaggle score may indicate that your validation strategy needs to change.

## Your final submissions

Choose the models for your final Kaggle submissions on your validation results, not on the public leaderboard: the public leaderboard scores only 100 of the 200 test molecules, and the final ranking uses the other half (see [The Kaggle competitions](../iteration-3/index.qmd#the-kaggle-competitions)).

## Write a short summary

End the project with a short summary of your work, for yourself or to share, for example in the course [Discussions](https://github.com/BredaUniversityADSAI/introduction-to-ml/discussions/categories/show-and-tell):

* your final models, their validation scores and their Kaggle scores;
* the experiments that made the biggest difference, and the ones that did not help;
* what you would try next with more time or more data.

The goal is no longer to follow instructions. The goal is to make increasingly well-informed machine-learning decisions and build the strongest solution you can.
